title: kbdecide.py lets an agent session record a tests-ceiling decision whose token has a prefix glued to it, which tests.py still accepts
goal: bl_authority.names_ceiling, which kbdecide.py's agent-session guard reads, matches every decision text that tests.py read_ceiling would accept for a ceiling (any text holding the ceiling token as a substring, such as 'ztests-ceiling ids=100 files=15 seconds=darwin:99'), so kbdecide.py record, confirm, supersede, restore and ratify refuse such a text from an agent session; the extended authority test plants the prefixed token and fails before the fix

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_authority as a;sys.exit(0 if all(a.names_ceiling(t) for t in ('ztests-ceiling ids=100 files=15 seconds=darwin:99','x_tests-ceiling ids=1 files=1 seconds=darwin:1')) else 1)

notes: Found by the SP-rlincemn review (finding 1). Premise run 2026-10-12 on origin/main 0aa024b61: names_ceiling('ztests-ceiling ids=1') is False while tests.py read_ceiling accepts any decision text holding the token as a substring (token in text). The suite is at 100 of 100 ids: extend the existing kbdecide authority test, add no id.
